business_summary.text: Gallantt Ispat is an integrated steel producer making TMT bars, billets, sponge iron and pellets, with units at Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh) and Kutch (Gujarat).

call_points.text: Gorakhpur capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tons expected to be operational in November 2026.
Captive solar plants expected to save ₹30 crores to ₹40 crores annually in power cost.
TMT prices in September were about 21% higher than a year ago amid strong domestic demand.
Domestic steel demand expected to grow 7-9% this year; Q1 and Q2 muted by monsoon, recovery from Q3.
Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes on course for commissioning in H2FY27.
Of the ₹3,000 Cr capex, about ₹800 Cr spent; roughly half goes to mining development, the rest to solar and capacity.
All three captive iron ore mines (two UP, one Rajasthan) targeted operational in FY28.
Company holds more than 25% market share in UP from the addressable market; Janhvi Kapoor added as second brand celebrity.
Net debt-free as of June 30, 2026; borrowings limited to working capital; capex funded by internal accruals.
Kutch rolling mill utilisation at 66% versus Gorakhpur's 93%; improving it is a Q2 focus.
Management does not expect substantial EBITDA erosion for the full year despite fuel and freight pressure.

operating_notes.text: Promoters voluntarily waived off right to receive FY26 final dividend of ₹2/share to retain funds for ongoing expansion.
FY26 production: pellets 819 kt, sponge iron 915 kt, billet 883 kt, TMT bar 788 kt; sales: pellet 49 kt, sponge iron 125 kt, billet 81 kt, TMT bar 766 kt.
Raw material cost held at about 72% of net realisation in both FY25 and FY26.
Capacity utilisation at 88%, with 90-92% seen as a good level; about 25% market share in its UP and Gujarat selling areas.
As on 31 March 2026, promoters and promoter group held 16,89,70,562 shares (70.031%) of Gallantt Ispat, with Gallantt Trust alone at 14,48,90,556 shares (60.051%) and nil shares pledged.
TMT bar sales volumes were about 192,000 tonnes in Q1FY27, flat YoY and down about 8% QoQ.
Kutch rolling mill utilisation was about 66% versus 93% at Gorakhpur in Q1FY27.
The pellet plant has an installed capacity of about 8 lakh tonnes and requires about 9 lakh to 9.5 lakh tonnes of raw feed annually; about 15-20% of the mix comes from Lloyds.
Group manufactures steel and allied products including pellet, sponge iron, ingots, and TMT Bars.
Q2 FY27 TMT sales volume was 1,65,000 tons compared to 1,92,000 tons in Q1 FY27.
Kutch rolling mill utilization was 68% in Q2 FY27 compared to 66% in Q1 FY27.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,204.81 Cr (+12.4% YoY), net profit ₹122.83 Cr (+5.6% YoY).
Gallantt Ispat Limited’s Board, chaired by **Nitesh Kumar**, recommended a final dividend of ₹2 per share (20% of ₹10 face value) on May 5, 2026, pending AGM approval.
Gallantt's first earnings call (6 May 2026) guided to ₹5,300-5,400 Cr revenue and ~20% margin after a ₹3,000 Cr capex: steel capacity to 1.3 mt in H2FY27, 78 MW solar, and ₹1,500 Cr of mines by FY28.
Promoters disclosed holding 16,89,70,562 shares, or 70.031% of Gallantt Ispat, as on 31 March 2026, with no new encumbrances during FY26.
On its Q1FY27 call (July 28, 2026), Gallantt reported revenue of ₹1,146 Cr (+2% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 18%, and said its 1.23 mt capacity expansion and 85 MW solar are on track for H2FY27.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,145.89 Cr (+13.1% YoY), net profit ₹60.51 Cr (-32.0% YoY).
Gallantt Ispat reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹1,145.89 Cr and PAT of ₹60.51 Cr, impacted by planned plant shutdowns and higher input costs.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval for final dividend of ₹2 per share
Shareholder approval for appointment of independent directors Sanjay Kumar Jain and Kishore Pariyar
EBITDA margin after expansion and mining
Mine approvals, which management says are still being worked on

watchlist.response: Management said surplus is deployed in the intercorporate market at 12%, payable on demand within three months, and it sees no counterparty risk.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked what the ₹294-297 Cr of loans on the balance sheet are

watchlist.response: Management could not give the percentage, saying only that it is 'not a very substantial percentage'.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked what percentage of power cost the solar savings represent
Environment and forest clearances for the two UP iron ore mines

watchlist.response: Said margins are in line with the yearly average of 17-18% and FY26 EBITDA per tonne of about ₹8,800 versus about ₹8,700 now, attributing the YoY fall to raw material pressure and the pellet shutdown.
watchlist.text: EBITDA per tonne fell YoY; is it a one-off from pellets or a structural raw material hit?

watchlist.response: Called the decline marginal at 2-2.5% and pointed to H2FY27 capacity additions for higher volumes; did not give a specific growth target.
watchlist.text: FY26 revenue grew only 2.9% against a five-year CAGR near 34%; why should Q1FY27 support a return to double-digit growth?
